/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 16-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department because of severe left flank pain and nausea for 3 hours. The pain is colicky and radiates towards his groin. He drinks multiple glasses of iced tea every day. He has had similar episodes of abdominal pain in the past. His maternal uncle has a similar history of abdominal pain. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 103/min, and blood pressure is 108/72 mm Hg. Examination shows a soft and nontender abdomen. Left costovertebral angle tenderness is present. An x-ray of the abdomen shows no abnormalities. A urinary cyanide nitroprusside test is positive. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following?

Options:
A. Rhomboid crystals on urinalysis
B. Urinary pH of 7.8
C. Serum anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies
D. Proteus mirabilis on urine culture
E. Hexagon-shaped crystals on urinalysis
